excerpts.text: The first sentence of Article 53 sets out the rule, namely, that peremptory norms allow for no contradiction by treaties, while the second sentence defines a peremptory norm of general international law for the purposes of the Convention.

There is a conflict, if the treaty, which is being concluded, cannot be performed in the future without breaching jus cogens. Impeachment of the treaty can be set in motion by any party to the treaty invoking the ground of invalidity in Article 53.

excerpts.text: In the final text of the Charter, distributed on October 11, Article 53 finally became Article 53.[60](#P278_69325) As mentioned earlier, the reference to "Union law" was reinserted at this late point.

The Council of Europe observers also submitted comments on the final text.[63](#P285_71828) They found that Article 52(3) in conjunction with Article 53 ensured "an identity of scope and meaning between the rights contained in the two instruments [Charter and ECHR], without preventing Union law from affording wider protection than that provided by the ECHR." The recognition of the ECHR as a minimum standard "is entirely compatible with the ECHR, Article 53 of which indicates that the ECHR is not intended to impose a uniform level of protection [...], but solely to ensure a minimum standard."
